You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "path": "memory/task-4b4c7538.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task-4b4c7538 solved (2026-10-22)

## Rule
Input contains a solid rectangle of color 2 and sparse same-color-as-each-other marker cells (test markers are 1; demo markers 8, 3, 4). Extend color 2 from the rectangle in straight horizontal/vertical lines in the rows/columns specified by these markers, respecting directionality: a marker outside the rectangle on one side blocks extension toward that marker, while extension proceeds away from it; where a direction is unblocked, extend to the grid boundary. Preserve all marker cells and zeros not on extensions. The rectangle itself remains intact.

Operationally infer extensions independently for each of the rectangle's rows and columns. A marker aligned with a rectangle row/column signals that line's directional constraint; markers on the opposite side block that direction, so fill from rectangle edge toward the other grid edge. Without an aligned blocking marker, line extensions can go to both grid edges. Demos demonstrate some extension segments are excluded / interrupted around relevant marker columns/rows, so carefully compare marker alignment and side before building output.

## Demo evidence
- Demo 2: 20x15, rectangle color 2 rows 5-9 cols 4-8 (0-based). Sparse color-3 markers outside. Output extended 2s horizontally across grid for rectangle rows, with directional limits associated with markers; also extended vertical color-2 stripes above/below rectangle in selected columns. Original markers preserved.
- Demo 3: 20x17, rectangle rows 4-9 cols 5-10. Output has horizontal extensions across rows and vertical extensions in selected columns; marker color 4 cells remain visible. Example row 5 and row 6 extend across the entire width, while a marker on row 9 at far right corresponds to extension leftward but not through its marker; likewise vertical output follows marked columns.
- Demo 1: 21x25, rectangle rows 1-8 cols 2-9. Same rule, with long horizontal and vertical colored lines.

Test had 20x20, color-2 rectangle rows 2-8 cols 9-15 (0-based); marker 1 locations: (r2,c6), (r3,c19), (r4,c5), (r7,c1), (r8,c19), (r12,c9), (r17,c13), (r19,c15).
